summary: A request from MITRE for ARPA sites to help Georgetown University's library system. Sites could share an existing library retrieval system or the community could design a network library information system, possibly with a working group.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC asks network organizations whether they can share a library retrieval system with Georgetown or help design a shared system. The goal would include searching other libraries' holdings and arranging inter-library loans.

questions: what was the network library information system proposal
how could network libraries support inter library loans
subtitle: A request to explore sharing library retrieval systems across the network.

tldr.problem: Georgetown University was designing a Learning Resource Center and considering online queries of its library holdings.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC asks whether a site can share an existing library retrieval system or whether the network community should design a shared system and protocols.
tldr.outcome: The notice seeks interest in sharing, using or designing a network library information system; it does not define one.

today: RFC 286 is a proposal to explore library information sharing published in December 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Georgetown's Library Query Need
sections.content:
Georgetown University was designing a Learning Resource Center that might include an online way to query the university's library holdings. The RFC asks the ARPA community whether it could help.

One possibility was for an organization to share an existing Library Retrieval System with Georgetown.
sections.plainLanguage: Georgetown was considering an online system for searching its library holdings. The RFC asks whether another organization could share a system it already had.

sections.title: A Network Library Information System
sections.content:
The RFC presents a second option: the ARPA community could design a Network Library Information System. The author notes that many organizations may need such a service and that users could benefit from searching other libraries and arranging inter-library loans.

If interest were sufficient, a working group could establish protocols and resolve system details. The NIC might contribute and possibly act as a focal point for design and operation.
sections.plainLanguage: Network organizations could work together on a shared library system. A working group could define protocols if enough organizations were interested.

sections.title: Request for Interest
sections.content: The RFC asks readers to contact the author if they know of a system that could be shared with Georgetown, if their organization wants to participate in a retrieval system, or if they want to help design one.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks organizations to report existing systems, interest in using one or willingness to help design it.
